# Atlas

> Atlas reads code (Python, Rust, TypeScript) into a graph of places where data rests, functions as arrows between them, and routes from entry points to places; it draws that graph, and `atlas check` asks ten design principles of it. A human and a coding agent share the picture: pointing at a box is a statement both can act on. Atlas never guesses: a place, a type or a call the code does not say is drawn as one it does not say.

The documents below are written to be read whole. Start with the design's first section, the shared language.

## Docs

- [Design](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raoulg/atlas/main/docs/reference/design.md): the shared language (places, arrows, composition, zoom as a quotient, filters as fibers), the algebra, how each language is read, and the views.
- [Principles](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raoulg/atlas/main/docs/reference/principles.md): the ten principles `atlas check` asks, each with its reasoning, its idioms, and what each language lets Atlas trace.
- [Guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raoulg/atlas/main/docs/reference/guide.md): how to read the picture, what Atlas reads in each language, entry points, `check`, `changes` and the MCP tools.

## Use

- `atlas view [repo]` draws a repository as one HTML file; `atlas check [repo] --json` gives the findings; `atlas changes [rev]` what an edit did to the routes; `atlas mcp` serves the tools `principles`, `check`, `explain`, `routes`, `route`, `view` and `changes` over stdio.

## Optional

- [The pairs](https://github.com/raoulg/atlas/tree/main/engine/tests/pairs): the same programs written carefully and carelessly, the tests that state what Atlas shows of each.
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raoulg/atlas/main/README.md)
